Cats can run up to 48 km/h. They only sweat through their paw pads. Each cat has its own unique meow. They can recognize your voice (and sometimes ignore it). Cats have five toes in front and four in the back. They groom themselves to stay clean and regulate body temperature. Their brains are surprisingly similar to humans. Cats can see in low light, but not total darkness. Slow blinking means they trust you. 5 Foods That Make Cats Live Longer These five foods are easy add-ons that can help your cat stay healthier for longer. Cooked salmon brings the good fats that support their heart and kidneys, eggs give them complete protein plus taurine for a strong heart and sharp eyes, and a little broccoli, watermelon, or strawberry adds vitamins, fiber, and water most cats don't get enough of. Always serve them cooked or seedless where it matters, in small amounts, and never raw. Keep in mind these are treats, not a full meal plan. A long, healthy life still comes mostly from a balanced cat food made for their age, fresh water every day, and regular vet checkups, with these foods as a little bonus on top. Introduce anything new slowly and in tiny portions, since even safe foods can upset their stomach if you give too much too fast. #cats #catcare #cathealth #catlovers #cattips
